Signalis is a game I will probably never forget for as long as I live. 

Expertly-crafted survival horror gameplay, unique presentation... and a tragic, intentionally bleary narrative that invites and demands you to look further. To fill in the blanks, to interpret its many themes, and to bridge gaps in a way you think works.

Transcendental game. Girls kiss.

Eldest Souls has some good aspects like the combat system, which you can change the way you fight with the skill trees. Also, bosses are well designed and challenge players in any way. The problem is the storytelling besides some hollow NPCs that can't bring anything special to the game.

Honestly, I don't know why Terraria has so many haters. This game literally has everything. Fun to play, tons of things to do, bosses to kill, ofc it has multiplayer so you can enjoy everything with friends, items to farm, a lot of stuff and decorations to build with, not to mention that if you hit the bottom and feel like you have completed the game, you can install some mods adding a crazy amount of new features, items, ect ...  When you're ingame (and I don't really know how to explain it) there's just something very chilling about it, maybe it's the music, maybe it's just every little detail about it. That's just how the game works. Perfect for chilling when you had a bad or exhausting day, but it's also the perfect entertainment for your free time. 10/10

Pretty fun boomer shooter with a cool comic book art style and a great Lovecraft-inspired atmosphere. The guns feel powerful, the combat is fast, and it does a good job of keeping the action entertaining.

It definitely has some flaws—enemy encounters can get repetitive, the difficulty be very overwhelming of enimies, and a few levels drag on longer than they should. Still, the strong art direction and satisfying gameplay make it easy to overlook those issues and make an enjoyable experience for anyone who enjoys old-school shooters.

Everybody already knows that this is the most immersive Far Cry with the best villain ever. But Ubisoft has abandoned it, or has even tried to kill it with a patch that makes the game crash every five minutes.
So, instead of giving it a negative review for being unplayable, I’ll just go straight to the 100% working solution:

https://github.com/ShonkV/Large-Address-Aware/releases/tag/V1.0

Download this application, open it, and select the Far Cry executable (FarCry.exe first (optional), and then FarCryDx11.exe for DX11), Check the box under LAA flag and Then simply click on save to make the game use more than 2 GB of RAM.

9/10 - Amazing

Game feels more like a DLC rather then a full fledged game. It sucks because there is so MUCH more that this game could have been. Buy on sale, game takes less then 4 hours to complete.

I didn't believe it was possible to improve on perfection but despite the immense pressure Bloober team was under... they did it! Silent Hill 2 remake is a masterpiece.
It's got new QOL and accessibility features, improved gameplay elements and combat, an updated OST (also made by the same composer who did the original games soundtrack), new and updated story elements (including new endings), new ways to approach puzzles, more open world exploration within Silent Hill and so much more, but most importantly it's still the same Silent Hill game at heart that we fell in love with over 20 years ago.

The remake is truly a remake done right. Soooo, Silent Hill 1 and 3 remakes when?

EDIT: I’ve now finished my first playthrough of the remake and it was absolute cinema, I cannot recommend the game enough! It. Is. PEAK!

Part real-time puzzle, part precision brawler, this roguelite has a really interesting premise - can you perfect your technique and your game plan, and NOT screw it up when it matters? 

FWIW I enjoy the gameplay more than any of the story bits, which tend to get in the way of my enjoyment. But very much liking this game.
The game is great, but I wish they had more unlockables, like my maybe a radio or something. Just neat little cosmetic things to work towards too.

I always found Shovel Knight to be good but a little flat, so I thought this would be just a typical cute link to the past/link's awakening like, but it's so much better than I expected. I was expecting a fairly standard and linear formula, eg. "Go here, clear this dungeon, get this upgrade, open up this path" etc. but the map and level structure, movement/combat, and RPG elements give it so much more depth. There's a crazy amount of room for player expression with all the different items you can equip. 

The movement feels a bit rigid at first (very NES feel,) but the more you lean into the mechanics, the more you realize how fluid it actually is. Many encounters can end up as this elegant dance that you'd expect to come out of devil may cry.

This is one of the best sequels I have ever played. The puzzles and game mechanics have been improved significantly, with new abilities and strategies to use. The story goes more in-depth than the first one, with many different chapters and sections to explore. There are many immersive opportunities to explore the past & present of the planet, alongside Mui's backstory! I enjoyed this game a lot (arguably more than the first one, which was also very enjoyable) and am excited for Planet of Lana III. Extreme kudos!
It gets a bit long and occasionally tedious with the amount of platforming puzzles, but it's a beautiful game.

Divinity Original Sin was a good game. Divinity Original Sin 2 was, in my opinion, the best top down RPG ever made at that point (I'm 72 and I have played a bunch of them). Baldur's Gate 3 is looking even more complex, has better graphics, better cut scenes, deeper interpersonal interactions and a better story line than Divinity Original Sin 2. L. Studios keeps improving. I have never paid for a Beta game before but I trusted that this game would be finished and I am certain that it will. Sans the understandable crashes, gliches and freezes, this game is truly fun to play even though it is not finished.

What can I say about this game that has not already been stated in other reviews? Let me start by saying this started out as an extremely fun platformer. It has a great art style and the music is great for this style of platformer. The game mechanics involve turning into a chicken (yes, that's right) and bouncing between the Land of the Living and the Land of the Dead while trying to wall jump and not fall. The problem is the game gets entirely way too difficult way too soon. I found myself screaming at my keyboard at moments. I can't remember the last time I felt so infuriated by the dificulty of a game. Don't get me wrong once you get past certain annoying parts this game has the bones to be one of the best platformers this year. My only advice to those who decide to play this game is to bring anti-anxiety medication along for the FUN but extremely DIFFICULT game. All the best!!

Mafia the old country is a bit of an odd-ball compared to previous games.

It is an open world game perse,  But limited to being forced to stick to the story area, with no real deviation in the world.
You can aquire horses, Cars and weapons,  But are forced to use the mission default loadout (some are 0 weapons)

The story and action sequences are fantastic, With the car races a highlight.

Overall i would give the game a 7 / 10 (wait for a 50% off at least)

A game that harkens back to the older 3D platformer games that were everywhere on PS2. Exploration is fun and rewarding, and scanning the local plantlife is pretty neat. It is short though, and the facial animation is atrocious, but if you are looking for something that is pretty easy going and looking for a little nostalgia, check this out.

The writing is kind of weak at the beginning, it gets a little better as you make your way through the game. The art style is not the same all the way through so you will find some models that almost fit but not quite. The controls could use a little bit more polish and have a tendency to get you into spots that you weren't aiming for. The platforming is really difficult for the casual gamer but there are checkpoints littered all over the place throughout the game so re-dos are overly abundant. Overall it's a pretty cute game. I would say it is worth somewhere around 4-6 USD. No achievements and very little replay value.
